title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: Information Centres (BILMERs) at local unions of tradesmen and craftsmen are established to support refugees' access to decent employment and raise their awareness on fundamental principles and rights at work. The services provided by BILMERs are improved by provision of trainings targeting BILMER staff for expanding their coverage of services to include refugee job-seekers and entrepreneurs, as well as increasing the number of staff available to provide such services, and 8 new BILMER Offices are opened in different cities. As of 2023, 10,752 refugees and host community members benefitted from counselling services, which focuses on fundamental labour rights, social cohesion, formal employment and decent work, provided by BILMERs. The technical capacities of inspection bodies of Social Security Institution (SSI) and Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MoLSS) strengthened through increased trainings to guide staff on how to consider specific issues concerning refugees in Turkish labour market to deliver more refugee-sensitive services. The increased capacity of labour market governance institutions contributed to the significant increases in the number of officially employed refugee and migrant workers from 91,500 in 2021 to 130,000 in 2022, including through simplified work permit procedures, improved inter-institutional integration and data exchange including through activation of a Protocol between Turkish Employment Agency, Social Security Institution (SSI) and DG for International Labour Force on Exchange of Refugee related labour market data to increase service delivery quality, and consideration of labour market related information on foreigners (including refugees) within the Annual Activity Reports of the SSI. Refugee workers benefited from the "legal aid" support that is typically available to Turkish workers to facilitate their access to National Labour Courts. Through the support of the German Development Bank (KfW), the ILO continues to support constituents in five municipalities (Mersin, Adana, Sanliurfa, Konya and Gaziantep) to provide improved inclusive and non-discriminatory services to promote decent work. The ILO conducted capacity-strengthening activities, with the support of the Government of the United States targeting provincial staff and frontline officers engaged in facilitating refugees' access to decent work within the provincial labour market context. From 2021-2023, 222 Social Security Auditors (SSI) and 26 SSI Experts benefited from capacity-building training. Key entities participated actively in these activities, including the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, the SSI, the Turkish Employment Agency, and the Directorate of Guidance and Inspection and resulted in a report, that provides policy recommendations on social security rights of refugees. ILO supported inter-institutional integration and data sharing between labour market governance institutions, supporting these institutions in matters such as statistics and identification and qualification determination. The ILO supported refugees' access to decent work opportunities through advocacy, bringing all relevant labour market actors together in provincial consultation workshops in 15 provinces to develop policy recommendations to overcome challenges faced by refugees in accessing decent work and services. Following the Protocol signed between the ILO and the Justice Academy in the Ministry of Justice, a series of trainings were carried out. The training program was delivered to 207 Labour Court Judges to provide a rights-based approach to access legal assistance, specifically focusing on refugees and migrant workers. To ensure the sustainability of the ILO efforts to promote refugees' access to justice and legal assistance, a ToT was delivered to a group of judges to enable them to continue the training activities within the institution.
